title: DEPTH=9 — same width as depth-10 winner, one fewer layer
description: Changed only DEPTH from 10 to 9 in train.py; model_dim stays 640 (5 heads, same as depth=10) due to HEAD_DIM=128 rounding, so this isolates layer count at fixed width.
reflection: val_bpb 0.998944, beats the DEPTH=10 baseline (1.002530) by ~0.0036 and is the new best result of the cell. Confirms the true optimum at model_dim=640 is fewer layers than 10 — the extra token throughput from one less layer outweighs the lost capacity within the fixed 5-min budget. Worth bracketing further: try DEPTH=7 or 8 at model_dim=640... but wait, DEPTH=8 gives model_dim=512 (base_dim=512, already multiple of 128), not 640 — so DEPTH=8 is a different width, already tested as the original baseline (1.014027), clearly worse. So the width=640 bracket is DEPTH 9/10 only (base_dim 576/640, both round to 640); DEPTH=9 is the smallest depth at this width. Going smaller (DEPTH=8) drops back to width=512. Next round should test whether width=640 with even fewer effective layers is possible another way, or move to a different axis (warmup, weight decay) at this new DEPTH=9 baseline.
